wins.text: Q4 revenue hit a record $7.7B, up 24% YoY; full-year revenue grew 14% to a record $25.8B
Data Center segment revenue grew 69% YoY to a record $3.9B in Q4, with full-year Data Center revenue nearly doubling (94% growth); Data Center AI revenue exceeded $5B for full year 2024
Client segment revenue grew 58% YoY to a record $2.3B in Q4; Client operating income surged to $446M (19% margin) from $55M (4% margin) a year ago
MI350 series silicon bring-up ahead of schedule — running large-scale LLMs within 24 hours of first silicon; production ramp pulled forward to mid-year from second half 2025
Record $14B of Embedded design wins closed in 2024, up more than 25% YoY; EPYC Turin launched with 540+ performance records across industry benchmarks

risks.text: Gaming segment revenue declined 59% YoY to $563M in Q4 due to semi-custom inventory normalization at Microsoft and Sony; Q1 2025 guidance calls for a significant further sequential decline in Gaming
Embedded segment revenue declined 13% YoY to $923M; demand environment remains mixed with softness in industrial and communications markets recovering slower than expected

Data Center GPU revenue was below server CPU revenue growth in Q4 (GPU grew less than the 9% sequential Data Center segment average), and first-half 2025 GPU revenue is guided roughly flat vs. second-half 2024, implying a near-term air pocket ahead of MI350 ramp
Q1 2025 revenue guided to ~$7.1B, down ~7% sequentially, with Data Center, Client, and Embedded all expected to decline sequentially due to seasonality

Competitive intensity in server CPU market is increasing, with analysts flagging potential pricing aggression from Intel and growing custom silicon from hyperscalers threatening AMD's 50%+ share at major cloud customers

guidance_items.detail: Q1 2025 revenue guided to ~$7.1B +/- $300M, up ~30% YoY but down ~7% sequentially; full-year 2025 expected to deliver strong double-digit percentage revenue growth YoY
Q1 2025 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~54%, consistent with Q4 2024; expected to step up in second half 2025 as Data Center mix increases
Full-year 2025 EPS expected to grow at a faster rate than revenue (strong double-digit percentage), building on 25% EPS growth in 2024
Gaming segment expected to decline significantly sequentially in Q1 2025; Embedded expected to decline modestly sequentially in Q1 2025
Q1 2025 non-GAAP opex ~$2.1B; non-GAAP other net income ~$24M; non-GAAP tax rate ~13%; diluted share count ~1.64B

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Specific Data Center GPU revenue breakdown for Q4 and Q1 (management declined to give explicit GPU-only figures, only segment-level)
Potential inventory buildup in Client segment given AMD's significant outperformance of the broader PC market in H2 2024
Competitive pricing aggression from Intel in server CPU market and threat from hyperscaler custom silicon to AMD's 50%+ cloud share
